results.detail: The same boundary label can admit different exclusion interpretations without a fixed semantic rule.
results.implication: The exclusion operator needs a frozen semantics or model class.

results.detail: A boundary can yield no admissible orientations.
results.implication: Failure semantics must distinguish invalid, empty, and resolved outcomes.

results.detail: An orientation family can be supplied without a boundary argument in an unconstrained model.
results.implication: The claimed dependency orientation <- boundary is not universal without an admissibility axiom.

results.detail: Distinct ordered orientations map to the same scalar.
results.implication: Scalar projection cannot define orientation identity.

results.detail: Removing context makes otherwise distinct relation instances indistinguishable in a repeated fixture.
results.implication: Context is semantically necessary where relation identity is reused.

results.detail: A self-loop orientation is its own inverse under role exchange.
results.implication: Non-identity of O and Inv(O) requires an explicit self-inverse exception.

results.detail: The same admissible aspect pair is permitted two distinct RT outputs.
results.implication: MTO single-valuedness requires an explicit selector or tie-break rule.

results.detail: Distinct aspect orderings resolve to the same order-insensitive RT representation.
results.implication: Historical aspect identity is not recoverable from RT output alone.

results.detail: A finite recursive transition graph contains a cycle.
results.implication: Domain termination cannot be assumed without a well-foundedness or stop condition.

results.detail: Set-valued OTM output erases repeated primitive occurrences.
results.implication: OTM must be multiset/sequence-valued when multiplicity is semantically relevant.

summary: Adversarial finite models expose unresolved semantic obligations for all three tested proposal families.
prohibited_inference: Countermodels to a declared candidate semantics do not by themselves falsify every possible formulation of the intake proposals.
